LitRadar third-party source and license notices

The first-party application is built in Go. The image's go-inventory directory
contains go.mod, go.sum, the actual module graph and binary build information,
toolchain settings, source hashes and retained module/Go license notices.
The local go-sdk patch and its source identity records are retained under
third_party in the repository and hashed in that inventory.

SQLite is linked through modernc.org/sqlite, a pure-Go translation of the
public-domain SQLite C source, with its modernc.org/libc runtime and related
modernc.org modules. All of their LICENSE* files, including LICENSE-SQLITE and
LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, are retained with the other module notices in that
inventory.

Obscura 0.2.4
Copyright the Obscura contributors. Licensed under Apache-2.0; see
Obscura-LICENSE.txt. The image distributes the unmodified official render and
stealth release binaries, including obscura-worker, from:
https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/releases/tag/v0.2.4

Dockerfile and obscura-release.json record the selected archives and checksums.
LitRadar does not compile or patch the bundled Rust/V8/ICU implementation.
The user waived Obscura supply-chain verification for this migration (A13).
The image SBOM records Obscura as an opaque upstream binary distribution; it
does not certify its transitive dependencies or license/source completeness.

Poppler's pdftotext and its libraries are installed from Ubuntu packages. Their
copyright and license notices remain under /usr/share/doc in the image.

Windows distributions use the versioned conda-forge binary repackaging from
https://github.com/oschwartz10612/poppler-windows, not an official Poppler Windows
release. windows-release.json records the exact archive and SHA-256. The archive's
original directory layout and included poppler-data notices are retained under
native/poppler-26.09.0. Microsoft VC runtime DLLs from that distribution are also
copied beside Obscura for app-local loading. The upstream archive does
not provide a complete transitive license inventory. Poppler source and license:
https://poppler.freedesktop.org/ ; packaging recipes and dependency sources:
https://github.com/conda-forge/poppler-feedstock .

Search tokenizer
----------------
The Go search tokenizer reimplements the byte rules of the simple 0 tokenizer
from https://github.com/wangfenjin/simple (MIT). No Simple source, library or
dictionary is distributed; SQLite indexes the Go tokens with the built-in FTS5
ascii tokenizer.
